title: Lets Build An Agent from Scratch — Kam Lasater
talk_summary: A from-scratch tutorial building a minimal agent in five steps: LLM call, LLM-as-judge condition, tool calls (including parallel), a to-do-list planning loop, and a prompt that drives the loop.

takeaways.technique: LLM-as-judge as a callable tool inside the agent loop
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of a separate gating step, the judge is exposed as a tool the agent must call ('check goal done'), so the loop is driven by the model itself and the judge returns a forced strict JSON boolean.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you always ask your assistant to check goal done that drives towards llm as judge

takeaways.technique: Explicit to-do list tools (add/mark-done/check) as agent memory
takeaways.what_they_do: The agent gets add_todo, mark_done, check_todos, check_done tools; the system prompt forces a plan before work and a summary from the to-do list at the end. This is the read/write memory plus loop condition.
takeaways.evidence_quote: before do any of your work you always make a plan to use your to-do list

takeaways.technique: Iteration guardrails on the tool loop
takeaways.what_they_do: Notes that an LLM can loop forever calling tools if context is pruned and no boundary is hit; recommends capping iterative loops before client code cuts it off.
takeaways.evidence_quote: some guardrails I've seen get put on or the number of uh iterative Loops that they're able to go through

takeaways.technique: Parallel tool calls with tool_call_id correlation
takeaways.what_they_do: Handles arrays of tool calls by Promise.all over them and pushes each response back with its tool_call_id so the model can trace which call produced which result.
takeaways.evidence_quote: this will have a tool call ID so that the llm is able to trace um I asked for this tool to be called

takeaways.what_they_do: Frames each tool as a simple text transformation (URL -> markdown, query -> results string) and keeps tool schemas hand-written and minimal with strict JSON.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the tools are are best handled by thinking of them as text Transformations
